messages:
Sasha: Quick heads up — ACME POC reporting ~2.5s TTFT on chat endpoint even with batching turned on. Theyre hitting it on short prompts (3-10 tokens) and it kills the demo flow. @Tom @Priya can you jump in?
Dana (ACME): repro steps: single call, payload ~200 tokens, but were seeing initial token take 2.3-2.7s. sometimes first token faster then spikes. no obvious 429s.
Tom: thanks Sasha. can you drop the raw request id and a sample response header? also which model and route config?
Sasha: route: redwood/chat-lambda v1 pinned, model: rw-chat-7b-v1. request id: req_0a9f3c. attaching customer note: "invoked with client-side concurrency 1, server batching enabled by default"
Dana (ACME): attaching logs (pasted):
```
[2025-11-03T15:12:09Z] req_0a9f3c START
[2025-11-03T15:12:11Z] batcher: queued 6 requests, forming batch
[2025-11-03T15:12:11Z] runtime: launched kernel, seq_len=8, tok_out=1
[2025-11-03T15:12:13Z] runtime: kv-cache miss for prefix checksum abc123
[2025-11-03T15:12:14Z] req_0a9f3c COMPLETE latency=2.4s
```
Tom: interesting — kv-cache miss + small sequences. small batched requests have higher per-request overhead. two things to check: (1) if client is adding ephemeral prompt metadata that prevents cache hits (prefix variance) and (2) batch scheduling causing queuing delays due to max_batch_size and queue_timeout.
Priya: also check that the batching policy isn't trying to fill to large batch sizes for short sequences; CPU/GPU kernel kickoff cost dominates for tiny seqs. we usually recommend preferring low-latency mode for demos.
Sasha: ok what are the immediate knobs we can flip for a POC (no infra changes)? customer is ok with config tweaks but not dedicated capacity yet.
Tom: short-term knobs:
- set route config: `prefer_low_latency: true` (forces greedy dispatch, smaller batches)
- set `max_batch_size: 8` and `queue_timeout_ms: 20`
- enable prefix KV caching with normalized prompt template (if possible)
Example API patch (curl):
```
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/chat-lambda/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"prefer_low_latency":true,"max_batch_size":8,"queue_timeout_ms":20}'
```
Priya: if they can normalize the prompt prefix (remove per-request timestamps/ids) we usually jump cache hit rate. also we can enable `kv_cache.prefetch: true` for this route to warm cache for repeated prefixes.
Dana (ACME): we do include a small per-request trace id in the prompt. can we keep it but still get cache hits?
Tom: trace id inside the prompt body will break prefix caching. two options: move trace id to request metadata/header (not in prompt) OR use a stable prefix template and append trace id after the cached region.
Sasha: pricing question from ACME: if we want to move to low-latency guaranteed slot for the POC (dedicated preemptible instance) what's the delta price for a 1-month eval?
Dana (ACME): were happy to pay for smoother demo.
Sasha: tagging finance/sales ops for numbers, but rough internal note — dedicated POC instance usually ~3-4x per-token cost but gives <200ms TTFT for short prompts. I'll confirm exact quote.
Tom: also filed an internal ticket to track this POC perf work: SLS-789. I'll escalate if we see more than 5% tail latency over SLA.
deploy-bot: "route patch applied" for chat-lambda at 2025-11-03T15:18:40Z
Sasha: applied Tom's config changes; Dana can you re-run the demo?
Dana (ACME): re-ran 6 calls, results: first-token latencies: 0.18s, 0.22s, 0.19s, 0.2s, 0.23s, 0.19s. huge improvement, thanks! :tada:
Priya: great — still follow-up items: (1) we should add a small evaluation to check cache hit ratio per-prefix, (2) add a short-lived dedicated slot for their high-velocity demo window if they want 99th percentile guarantees.
Sasha: noted. I'll ask customer to send security questionnaire for dedicated plan. Dana can you send over SOC/ISO contact details and well loop in privacy/compliance.
Dana (ACME): will do, sending now. thanks team!
Tom: leaving one more note: for production this pattern (tiny prompts + high QPS) tends to benefit from either prefix-caching + model quantization or a low-latency dedicated pool. happy to draft a recommended config doc for ACME POC.
Sasha: perfect — assigning follow-ups: Tom -> SLS-789 attach perf logs & config; Priya -> write mini-doc on prompt normalization; Sasha -> pricing quote and compliance contacts. closing thread once docs & quote are in place. :white_check_mark:
